messages.subject: Model projections for an ectotherm
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

Thanks a lot for getting me in the group!

First of all, I am rookie in mechanistic modelling approach, so please be patient. ;-)

I am trying to follow the ellipsoid endotherm model through my biophysical spatially explicit dataset and I wonder how can I get the final distribution map of any trait. After checking the functions help, I think there was not a function/tool to solve it yet, right? Is there any other example through a R code where to rasterize both the microclimatic variables and model trait predictions?

Many thanks in advance.
Salvador.

messages.subject: Re: Model projections for an ectotherm
messages.body_plain:
Hi Salvador,

You should look into faster based calculations in R. You can apply the ellipsiod model to e.g. a spatial grid of air temperature and wind speed values and map the consequences - e.g. the metabolic heat needed to stay at a given core temp. Can’t give you an example right now as I’m travelling but do some googling on apply functions and faster calculations in general.

All the best,
Mike

Re: micro_USA() function error
messages.body_plain:
Hi Michael,
    So I've had a bit more time to play around with the function on PC and Mac and found that I receive the same error if the site is anywhere east of the -100.00 longitude line for the US. West of the line it works well on Mac and with the modified ncdf4 package for PC (coast and inland). I've tried random locations using both decimal degrees and quotations around cities but run into the same issue for anything east of that line. The error appears to happen right after attempting to extract the 'tmin' weather input.

While searching for the error I saw something about the coordinate format (double vs. index) but I am pretty unfamiliar with the specifics/conversions.

Thanks for all your help,
Adam
